topic.title: Faithful Explanations and Explanation-Guided Learning
topic.overview: Explainable learning aims to show which information drives a model's prediction and to make those explanations useful. This cluster includes feature attribution, self-explaining architectures, explanation regularization, and free-text rationales. A representative method lets practitioners penalize inappropriate feature importance, turning an explanation into a training signal informed by domain knowledge.
topic.whyItMatters: An explanation can sound plausible without faithfully describing the model. Evaluating stability, sufficiency, and sensitivity to relevant inputs helps separate persuasive descriptions from evidence that supports correction or understanding.
topic.evolution: Early representatives concern learning from and reusing explanations. Later work focuses on neural attribution and training models to respect explanatory constraints. Recent studies extend sufficiency tests to language-model explanations and show that conclusions depend on the input distribution used to evaluate them.
openQuestions: How should an explanation's evaluation distribution be chosen?
When does optimizing explanation quality improve the underlying decision process rather than just its presentation?

papers.tldr: Describing neurons as linear combinations of concepts captures behavior missed by explanations based only on their strongest activations.

papers.title: Local Feature Selection without Label or Feature Leakage for Interpretable Machine Learning Predictions
papers.tldr: SUWR provides provably leakage-free local feature selection, making sparse prediction explanations less prone to hidden information encoding.

papers.title: Local vs. Global Interpretability: A Computational Complexity Perspective
papers.tldr: The relative difficulty of local and global explanations reverses across model families for the sufficient-subset task studied.

papers.title: On Gradient-like Explanation under a Black-box Setting: When Black-box Explanations Become as Good as White-box
papers.tldr: GEEX produces gradient-like feature explanations using only model queries, with proven attribution properties and competitive image results.

papers.title: Position: An Inner Interpretability Framework for AI Inspired by Lessons from Cognitive Neuroscience
papers.tldr: This position paper draws on cognitive neuroscience to propose a framework and methods for explaining AI systems’ internal mechanisms.

papers.title: Position: Explain to Question not to Justify
papers.tldr: This position paper calls for more explainability methods that investigate, validate, and repair models, alongside human- and value-oriented explanations.

papers.title: Post-hoc Part-Prototype Networks
papers.tldr: A post-hoc decomposition reconstructs a trained classifier’s head with interpretable part-prototypes, preserving performance while explaining what features matter and where.

papers.title: Probabilistic Conceptual Explainers: Trustworthy Conceptual Explanations for Vision Foundation Models
papers.tldr: PACE models patch concepts probabilistically to explain vision transformers across patch, image, and dataset levels.

papers.title: Prospector Heads: Generalized Feature Attribution for Large Models & Data
papers.tldr: Prospector heads improve localization of class-relevant input regions across text, pathology images, and protein graphs.

papers.title: Provably Better Explanations with Optimized Aggregation of Feature Attributions
papers.tldr: Optimizing convex combinations of feature attributions yields provable improvements in selected explanation criteria and strong experimental results.

papers.title: Saliency strikes back: How filtering out high frequencies improves white-box explanations
papers.tldr: FORGrad filters high-frequency gradient artifacts to improve existing white-box explanations while preserving their computational appeal.

papers.title: Towards Compositionality in Concept Learning
papers.tldr: CCE extracts concepts that combine more compositionally and improve downstream classification in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: Trust Regions for Explanations via Black-Box Probabilistic Certification
papers.tldr: The paper develops query-based methods to probabilistically certify regions where an existing model explanation satisfies a chosen quality criterion.

papers.title: TVE: Learning Meta-attribution for Transferable Vision Explainer
papers.tldr: TVE pretrains reusable attribution knowledge to explain different vision models and tasks without additional training on downstream data.

papers.title: Understanding Inter-Concept Relationships in Concept-Based Models
papers.tldr: The paper finds weaknesses in learned concept relationships and shows that using those relationships can improve concept intervention accuracy.

papers.title: Auditing Local Explanations is Hard
papers.tldr: Auditing local explanations through prediction-and-explanation queries can require prohibitively many queries, especially in high-dimensional settings.

papers.title: CoSy: Evaluating Textual Explanations of Neurons
papers.tldr: CoSy evaluates neuron descriptions by generating examples from the text and comparing neuron responses against control examples.

papers.title: Data-faithful Feature Attribution: Mitigating Unobservable Confounders via Instrumental Variables
papers.tldr: Instrumental-variable training separates hidden confounder effects from input contributions to produce more data-faithful feature attributions.

papers.title: Explanations that reveal all through the deﬁnition of encoding
papers.tldr: A formal definition of explanation encoding leads to STRIPE-X, which distinguishes transparent explanations from those carrying extra predictive information.

papers.title: Human Expertise in Algorithmic Prediction
papers.tldr: The framework identifies when experts add information beyond a predictor and selectively uses their judgments to improve predictions.

papers.title: Improving Decision Sparsity
papers.tldr: The paper extends Sparse Explanation Value with flexible references and feature-space distances to produce sparser, more meaningful decision explanations.

papers.title: Interpretable Mesomorphic Networks for Tabular Data
papers.tldr: Mesomorphic networks use deep hypernetworks to generate interpretable linear models for individual tabular inputs while retaining strong empirical accuracy.

papers.title: Measuring Per-Unit Interpretability at Scale Without Humans
papers.tldr: An automated interpretability measure enables analysis of over 70 million vision-network units and reveals a negative association with classification performance.

papers.title: Model Reconstruction Using Counterfactual Explanations: A Perspective From Polytope Theory
papers.tldr: A geometry-informed training loss uses counterfactual explanations’ proximity to decision boundaries to improve model reconstruction.

papers.title: Navigating the Maze of Explainable AI: A Systematic Approach to Evaluating Methods and Metrics
papers.tldr: LATEC shows how conflicting explanation metrics can produce unreliable rankings and provides a broader benchmark and more robust evaluation scheme.

papers.title: Optimal ablation for interpretability
papers.tldr: Optimal ablation provides theoretically and empirically advantageous component-importance estimates that benefit several interpretability tasks.

papers.title: Selective Explanations
papers.tldr: Selective explanations detect inaccurate fast feature attributions and selectively refine them to balance explanation quality with computation.

papers.title: shapiq: Shapley Interactions for Machine Learning
papers.tldr: shapiq unifies algorithms, visualizations, and benchmarks for explaining individual and joint contributions with Shapley methods.

papers.title: Testing Semantic Importance via Betting
papers.tldr: The paper formalizes semantic concept importance using conditional independence and applies sequential testing to rank concepts relevant to black-box predictions.

papers.title: Utilizing Human Behavior Modeling to Manipulate Explanations in AI-Assisted Decision Making: The Good, the Bad, and the Scary
papers.tldr: Learned models of human decision-making can guide explanation changes that influence users, often without users noticing.

papers.title: xMIL: Insightful Explanations for Multiple Instance Learning in Histopathology
papers.tldr: xMIL improves explanations of histopathology models through a broader multiple-instance framework and layer-wise relevance propagation.

papers.title: A New Approach to Backtracking Counterfactual Explanations: A Unified Causal Framework for Efficient Model Interpretability
papers.tldr: BRACE uses backtracking counterfactuals and causal reasoning to generate efficient, actionable explanations of model decisions.

papers.title: Beyond Topological Self-Explainable GNNs: A Formal Explainability Perspective
papers.tldr: A formal analysis exposes limitations of graph explanations and motivates a dual-channel model that also extracts concise rules.

papers.title: COMRECGC: Global Graph Counterfactual Explainer through Common Recourse
papers.tldr: COMRECGC explains graph classifications through compact sets of shared transformations that change rejected graphs into accepted ones.

papers.title: Enhancing Performance of Explainable AI Models with Constrained Concept Refinement
papers.tldr: Constrained concept refinement improves explainable models’ accuracy while preserving interpretability and reducing computation in reported image-classification evaluations.

papers.title: Evaluating Neuron Explanations: A Unified Framework with Sanity Checks
papers.tldr: A unified analysis and two sanity checks reveal that many neuron-explanation metrics ignore major label changes, motivating more reliable evaluation practices.

papers.title: Explaining, Fast and Slow: Abstraction and Refinement of Provable Explanations
papers.tldr: Reduced network abstractions speed up formally sufficient explanations, with refinement adding detail when the smaller network cannot verify them.

papers.title: ExpProof : Operationalizing Explanations for Confidential Models with ZKPs
papers.tldr: ExpProof explores proof-compatible versions of LIME to make explanations more usable when models are confidential and parties have conflicting interests.

papers.title: Fast Estimation of Partial Dependence Functions using Trees
papers.tldr: FastPD efficiently and consistently estimates partial dependence for tree models, supporting feature effects and higher-order interactions.

papers.title: FastCAV: Efficient Computation of Concept Activation Vectors for Explaining Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: FastCAV extracts concept activation vectors much faster while preserving similar performance and equivalent explanation insights in the reported applications.

papers.title: GEFA: A General Feature Attribution Framework Using Proxy Gradient Estimation
papers.tldr: GEFA estimates gradients in a proxy space to explain black-box models and produce unbiased Shapley Value estimates.

papers.title: LIMEFLDL: A Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations Approach for Label Distribution Learning
papers.tldr: LIMEFLDL adapts local black-box explanations to label distributions, accounting for label dependencies and analyzing explanation stability.

papers.title: One Wave To Explain Them All: A Unifying Perspective On Feature Attribution
papers.tldr: Wavelet-based attribution explains influential input structures by location and scale, matching or outperforming compared gradient-based methods across several modalities.

papers.title: Optimal Information Retention for Time-Series Explanations
papers.tldr: ORTE learns time-series explanation masks using an information-based objective that balances removing irrelevant patterns with retaining important ones.

papers.title: Position: Rethinking Explainable Machine Learning as Applied Statistics
papers.tldr: The authors propose treating model explanations as statistical quantities whose interpretation must be connected explicitly to the questions people want answered.

papers.title: Redundancy Undermines the Trustworthiness of Self-Interpretable GNNs
papers.tldr: Redundant explanations undermine self-interpretable GNNs, while a simple ensemble strategy can mitigate their inconsistency and inaccuracy.

papers.title: Representations Shape Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Theoretical Insights and Empirical Predictions
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes weak-to-strong learning through model representations and derives a label-free metric that predicts performance trends.

papers.title: Sum-of-Parts: Self-Attributing Neural Networks with End-to-End Learning of Feature Groups
papers.tldr: SOP learns feature groups end to end to give differentiable models built-in explanations with strong reported predictive performance.

papers.title: Towards Robustness and Explainability of Automatic Algorithm Selection
papers.tldr: A graph-based algorithm selector reconstructs suitable algorithm features to improve robustness to marginal shifts and explain its decisions.

papers.title: What makes an Ensemble (Un) Interpretable?
papers.tldr: The computational difficulty of explaining ensembles depends jointly on component count, size, and type, with sharply different results for trees and linear models.

papers.title: X-Hacking: The Threat of Misguided AutoML
papers.tldr: Automated model search can exploit equally accurate models to produce preferred explanations, a practice the paper calls X-hacking.

papers.title: Additive Models Explained: A Computational Complexity Approach
papers.tldr: Explaining additive models can be computationally easy or hard depending on the input domain, component models, task, and explanation method.

papers.title: Capturing Polysemanticity with PRISM: A Multi-Concept Feature Description Framework
papers.tldr: PRISM improves automated feature explanations by allowing a language-model neuron to receive descriptions covering multiple distinct concepts.

papers.title: CHiQPM: Calibrated Hierarchical Interpretable Image Classification
papers.tldr: CHiQPM combines hierarchical explanations with calibrated prediction sets while retaining high point accuracy.

papers.title: Correcting misinterpretations of additive models
papers.tldr: PatternGAM and PatternQLR correct misleading feature importance caused by suppressor variables in additive and polynomial models.

papers.title: DePass: Unified Feature Attributing by Simple Decomposed Forward Pass
papers.tldr: DePass traces Transformer feature contributions through one decomposed forward pass without auxiliary training.

papers.title: DEXTER: Diffusion-Guided EXplanations with TExtual Reasoning for Vision Models
papers.tldr: DEXTER uses generated images and language models to explain visual classifiers’ class-level behavior without training data or ground-truth labels.

papers.title: DiCoFlex: Model-Agnostic Diverse Counterfactuals with Flexible Control
papers.tldr: DiCoFlex generates diverse counterfactual explanations in one pass while letting users change constraints at inference time without retraining.

papers.title: ElliCE: Efficient and Provably Robust Algorithmic Recourse via the Rashomon Sets
papers.tldr: ElliCE produces recourse recommendations guaranteed to work across an ellipsoidal approximation of near-optimal models.

papers.title: FaCT: Faithful Concept Traces for Explaining Neural Network Decisions
papers.tldr: FaCT builds traceable concept explanations into a neural network while retaining competitive image-classification performance.

papers.title: GnnXemplar: Exemplars to Explanations - Natural Language Rules for Global GNN Interpretability
papers.tldr: GnnXemplar turns representative graph nodes and their neighborhoods into natural-language rules explaining class-level GNN behavior.

papers.title: Improving Perturbation-based Explanations by Understanding the Role of Uncertainty Calibration
papers.tldr: ReCalX improves perturbation-based explanations by recalibrating model confidence while preserving original predictions.

papers.title: LeapFactual: Reliable Visual Counterfactual Explanation Using Conditional Flow Matching
papers.tldr: LeapFactual uses conditional flow matching to generate meaningful visual counterfactuals, including for nondifferentiable and human-in-the-loop systems.

papers.title: Minimizing False-Positive Attributions in Explanations of Non-Linear Models
papers.tldr: PatternLocal transforms local explanation weights to reduce misleading attributions from suppressor variables while preserving local fidelity.

papers.title: OrdShap: Feature Position Importance for Sequential Black-Box Models
papers.tldr: OrdShap separates the influence of feature values from their sequence positions when explaining black-box predictions.

papers.title: Preserving Task-Relevant Information Under Linear Concept Removal
papers.tldr: SPLINCE removes linear concept predictability while exactly preserving target-label covariance and minimizing representation distortion.

papers.title: Probabilistic Stability Guarantees for Feature Attributions
papers.tldr: Soft stability and a model-agnostic certification algorithm provide interpretable attribution guarantees while supporting a better accuracy-stability trade-off with mild smoothing.

papers.title: Regional Explanations: Bridging Local and Global Variable Importance
papers.tldr: R-LOCO explains predictions using regional feature importance to address faithfulness failures identified in Local Shapley Values and LIME.

papers.title: Representational Difference Explanations
papers.tldr: RDX discovers and visualizes meaningful differences between two models' learned representations.

papers.title: Revising and Falsifying Sparse Autoencoder Feature Explanations
papers.tldr: Close negative examples and iterative structured explanations improve evaluation of sparse-autoencoder features.

papers.title: Robust Explanations of Graph Neural Networks via Graph Curvatures
papers.tldr: Graph curvature and resistance provide theoretical bounds and practical improvements for the robustness of graph-neural-network explanations.

papers.title: SHAP Meets Tensor Networks: Provably Tractable Explanations with Parallelism
papers.tldr: Tensor-network structure enables exact SHAP algorithms, with strong parallel-time guarantees for tensor trains and tractability at fixed network width.

papers.title: SHAP values via sparse Fourier representation
papers.tldr: A reusable sparse Fourier representation enables fast SHAP computation, with exact attribution summation and a tunable approximation trade-off for black-box models.

papers.title: The Non-Linear Representation Dilemma: Is Causal Abstraction Enough for Mechanistic Interpretability?
papers.tldr: Arbitrarily powerful alignment maps can make causal abstraction uninformative, so mechanistic interpretation needs assumptions about how models encode information.

papers.title: A Positive Case for Faithfulness: LLM Self-Explanations Help Predict Model Behavior
papers.tldr: Self-explanations help predict LLM behavior better than external explanations in the reported evaluation, although a meaningful minority are seriously misleading.

papers.title: Aggregate Models, Not Explanations: Improving Feature Importance Estimation
papers.tldr: Combining models before explaining them can improve feature-importance accuracy by reducing a leading error term associated with excess predictive risk.

papers.title: Beyond Additive Decompositions: Interpretability Through Separability
papers.tldr: Tensor Separation Learning models feature interactions through separable products while supporting faithful reconstruction from first-order partial dependence functions.

papers.title: CB-SLICE: Concept-Based Interpretable Error Slice Discovery
papers.tldr: CB-SLICE discovers groups of model errors through shared concept prediction failures, producing explanations tied directly to a concept bottleneck model’s predictions.

papers.title: Density-Guided Robust Counterfactual Explanations on Tabular Data under Model Multiplicity
papers.tldr: DensityFlow generates more robust counterfactual explanations by steering changes through well-supported data regions and using local surrogates to reduce black-box queries.

papers.title: ECSEL: Explainable Classification via Signomial Equation Learning
papers.tldr: ECSEL learns compact mathematical classifiers that offer competitive accuracy and directly inspectable explanations.

papers.title: ExPLAIND: Unifying Model, Data, and Training Attribution to Study Model Behavior
papers.tldr: ExPLAIND jointly attributes model behavior to components, data, and training history, revealing distinct learning dynamics in two case studies.

papers.title: Explanations are a Means to an End: Decision Theoretic Explanation Evaluation
papers.tldr: A decision-theoretic framework evaluates explanations by their potential, additional, and realized value for a specified decision task.

papers.title: Exposing Vulnerabilities in Explanation for Time Series Classifiers via Dual-Target Attacks
papers.tldr: TSEF induces targeted time-series misclassifications while preserving reference-consistent explanations, showing that explanation stability can conceal decision failures.

papers.title: Guaranteed Optimal Compositional Explanations for Neurons
papers.tldr: The framework guarantees optimal neuron explanations within its assumed search space and exposes suboptimal results from beam search.

papers.title: Hidden in Plain Sight – Class Competition Focuses Attribution Maps
papers.tldr: Considering attribution across competing classes makes existing explanation methods more focused, with reported benchmark gains of up to twofold.

papers.title: Hide&Seek: Learning to Explain in an End-to-End Differentiable Network
papers.tldr: Hide&Seek learns per-example feature explanations through differentiable partial feature replacement, jointly training selection and prediction without information leakage.

papers.title: Learn from A Rationalist: Distilling Intermediate Interpretable Rationales
papers.tldr: REKD improves smaller rationale-extraction models by teaching them both a stronger model’s feature selections and its predictions.

papers.title: MAnchors: Memorization-Based Acceleration of Anchors via Rule Reuse and Transformation
papers.tldr: MAnchors accelerates rule-based explanations by adapting and refining remembered intermediate rules while maintaining fidelity and understandability.

papers.title: Mixture of Concept Bottleneck Experts
papers.tldr: Mixture of Concept Bottleneck Experts varies the number and form of concept-based prediction rules to explore the accuracy-interpretability trade-off.

papers.title: Modeling Attributional Style at Scale: A Dataset and Analysis for Psychological Attribution Assessment and Reframing
papers.tldr: ASTD supplies specialist-validated attribution data and evaluation methods that support improved language-model assessment and reframing of explanatory styles.

papers.title: On the Variability of Concept Activation Vectors
papers.tldr: Theory and experiments indicate that Concept Activation Vector variance decreases roughly inversely with the number of random examples used.

papers.title: Optimal Transport Group Counterfactual Explanations
papers.tldr: Learned optimal transport maps generate reusable group counterfactuals while preserving group geometry and keeping movement costs competitive.

papers.title: Position: Explainability Research Must Prioritize Foundations over Ad-hoc Methods
papers.tldr: Explainability research should clarify its goals and build feedback workflows that turn explanations into useful human action.

papers.title: Position: Explanation Stability Is a Property of the Model–Method Pair, Not the Model
papers.tldr: Chest X-ray experiments show reversed explanation-stability rankings across attribution methods, supporting evaluation of model–method pairs.

papers.title: Position: In Defense of Information Leakage in Concept-based Models
papers.tldr: When concepts are incomplete, some leakage can support accurate, intervenable models, motivating a training objective that encourages benign leakage.

papers.title: Position: Interpretability Can Be Actionable
papers.tldr: Interpretability should be evaluated by how concretely and credibly its insights enable useful decisions and interventions.

papers.title: Position: Use Sparse Autoencoders to Discover Unknowns
papers.tldr: Sparse autoencoders may be especially useful for discovering unknown concepts even when they are less effective at acting on known ones.

papers.title: Prototype-Grounded Concept Models for Verifiable Concept Alignment
papers.tldr: Visual prototypes make learned concepts inspectable and correctable while preserving predictive performance comparable to leading concept bottleneck models.

papers.title: Sparse and Faithful Local Explanations with Piecewise Linear Surrogates
papers.tldr: PL-LIME uses sparse piecewise linear feature effects to produce more faithful and stable local explanations than LIME in reported experiments.

papers.title: Unified Time Series Explanations via Amortized Optimization and Instance-level Multi-Expert Knowledge Distillation
papers.tldr: XMA learns a fast time-series explainer from instance-specific expert choices and directly optimizes explanation faithfulness and robustness.

papers.title: What is Missing? Explaining Neurons Activated by Absent Concepts
papers.tldr: Simple extensions to explanation methods reveal neurons activated by missing concepts and can improve debiasing.

papers.title: What LLMs Explain Is Not What They Believe: Evaluating Explanation Sufficiency Under Models’ Own Input Beliefs
papers.tldr: SCSuff evaluates explanation sufficiency under a model’s own input beliefs and finds that tested LLM explanations are generally insufficient.
